newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bund futures turn positive in late trade.
newsitem.headline: German Bund futures turn positive in late trade.

text.p: German Bund futures recouped losses late in the session to finish in positive territory after a day of dull trade.
Traders said dealings were light with the U.S. market on holiday and a lack of news about German economic fundamentals.
The September Bund DTB future was up seven basis points at 97.25, near its high for the day.
Traders said from a chart standpoint, the market held up well, quickly recovering after briefly falling below chart support at 97.08.
Traders said a sustained breach below that level could have paved the for further losses. "The 96.70/80 level would be the next point after that for me," one trader said.
Despite the dull day, Bunds continued to outperform their U.S. counterparts. The Bund/T-note spread widened out slightly to minus 66 basis points from minus 65 basis points.

Traders said Bunds could outperform other European markets with several countries hammering out budgets. Indications of larger-than-expected deficits could spur a flight into the relative safty of German debt, they said.
